footnotes.text: Exodus 25:8. The Hebrew word translated as “dwell” refers to a temporary residence. The tabernacle was likely not understood to be God’s permanent dwelling, but rather a place where He could reside while communing with His people (see Daniel L. Belnap, “‘That I May Dwell among Them’: Liminality and Ritual in the Tabernacle,” inAscending the Mountain of the Lord: Temple, Praise, and Worship in the Old Testament, ed. David Rolph Seely and others (2013), 14.

See Bible Dictionary, “Shewbread”; see alsoLeviticus 24:8–9. The loaves likely represented a sacred meal offered to the Lord (see Richard Neitzel Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament: An Illustrated Reference for Latter-day Saints[2009], 106).
Tremper Longman III and Mark L. Strauss,The Baker Expository Dictionary of Biblical Words(2023), “Bread,” 118.

SeeDoctrine and Covenants 84:18, 24–27;107:1–6. The Lord provided the Aaronic Priesthood because the Israelites failed to observe the higher law administered under the authority of the Melchizedek Priesthood.

Although Aaron was the high priest, “Moses presided over Aaron because Moses held the Melchizedek Priesthood” (Boyd K. Packer, “The Aaronic Priesthood,”Ensign, Nov. 1981, 30). After the time of Aaron, the high priest was selected from among the firstborn descendants of Aaron and his sons (see Guide to the Scriptures, “High Priest,” Gospel Library).

Sister J. Anette Dennis, First Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency, taught: “As members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, those of us who have chosen to make covenants with God in the house of the Lord wear sacred ceremonial outer clothing during temple worship, symbolic of the clothing worn in ancient temple rituals. We also wear the garment of the holy priesthood, both during temple worshipandin our everyday lives” (“Put Ye On the Lord Jesus Christ,”Liahona, May 2024, 11). To learn more about the sacred clothing associated with temple ordinances in our day, see “Sacred Temple Clothing,”ChurchofJesusChrist.org.
